name: OnTimeSydney
question: How on time are Sydney's buses, really?
summary: Sets up a pipeline to capture Sydney bus GTFS-Realtime data and compare what was observed with what was predicted and scheduled. It is at the foundation stage (v0.1) and no data has been collected yet. The collector is next.

details.statusNote: Foundation stage (v0.1). No data has been collected yet, so there are no findings to show.
overview: Sydney buses report themselves on time more often than they are, and the data needed to check that disappears unless it is captured continuously.
OnTimeSydney captures GTFS-Realtime data from Transport for NSW and compares observed, predicted and scheduled times, so reliability can be measured honestly.

architecture.summary: A collector lands raw data as Parquet, loads it into PostgreSQL, and dbt models it from staging through intermediate to marts, feeding a report.

practices: CI runs lint, tests and a repository check on every push (make check).
pytest suites are split into unit and integration tests.
ruff handles linting and formatting, with its version pinned.
Pre-commit hooks block large files and private keys.
Rule: figures in the README must be generated by the pipeline, never typed by hand.

data.licence: CC BY 4.0, as stated in the project README

limitations: No data has been collected yet.
Known limitations are not documented yet; the README says they will be added as they are found.

headings.how: The design: a collector feeds Parquet, PostgreSQL and three dbt layers
headings.verify: CI runs lint, tests and a repository check on every push, before any data exists
headings.next: Next is the collector, then loading, modelling and metrics
